critical_changes: Correct the headline 'Texture is the least shared feature family' (Intro bullet 5, Section 5.5 heading/text). Per Table 6 it holds in only 3/6 configurations (GPT Image 1, Flare, FLUX.2 Max) plus SD-Turbo; spatial is lowest for GPT Image 2 (59.6%) and Sunburst (61.5%), and texture is the MOST shared family for Nano Banana 2 (79.8%).

Replace leave-one-scene deletion ranges as the only spread for headline shared fractions (Table 1, Section 5.1, Figure 3, Table 2) with scene-bootstrap or jackknife intervals for observed and faithful fractions and their difference. Deletion ranges understate scene variability by about sqrt(n-1): e.g., FLUX.2 Max 86.1-90.2% deletion range against a bootstrap interval of about 77.6-94.2%. Qualify 'a faithful imitator would share more' and the Figure 3 caption for FLUX.2 Max in the 31 features (88.4 vs 90.4; reversed in about 15% of paired scene resamples).

Narrow the abstract/intro claim that proximity gain would be mostly shared 'for a generator that reproduced each painter exactly'. The faithful benchmark includes the photographed-painting/generated-image domain gap, and the CSD GPT Image 2 faithful share is 48.3% (<50%). Add a domain-gap-free benchmark (observed shared term plus exact reference differences: S_obs/(S_obs+H/4) in embeddings, N/(N+H) in features; about 60.6-73.0% CLIP, 52.5-67.4% CSD, 57.6-84.2% features) and state the general condition under which the shared term dominates.

Report the prespecified family-level beta/D sensitivity (color, spatial, texture, without texture; present in psv2 analysis.json 'sensitivities' but absent from the paper), and revise the Section 5.6 list of analyses under which FLUX.2 Max keeps the lowest D: in the texture family Nano Banana 2 is lower (0.886 vs 0.906).

Reword 'movement toward the four painters' common appearance' (Section 6, Section 5.1) as movement toward the centroid of these reproductions, which the design identifies; align the abstract's opening 'for related painters' with the single four-painter, single-template scope.
minor_changes: Define the proximity readout precisely: mean image-to-reference cosine with unnormalized prototypes mu_a, distinct from the normalized prototypes used for recognition; note Eq. 4 holds for any linear score (normalized-prototype shares differ by at most 0.5 points).
Section 5.2 'the observed shares are only a few points higher': GPT Image 2 CLIP observed is lower (73.2 vs 76.0); gaps range -2.8 to +6.6 points.

Add intervals (scene and reference resampling) or an explicit point-description label to painter-pair beta/D (Figure 4, Table 14) and the 31-feature vs embedding Monet-Sisley contrast; e.g., Sunburst Monet-Sisley beta -0.249 has reference-resampling interval about [-0.45, 0.21].
Consider a two-way (scene x reference) bootstrap for D relative to 1, especially for the FLUX.2 Max below-1 statement.
Clarify the interval estimand (conservative for the fixed authored panel; not justified for a scene population) and interpret the 0.04% shared-state coverage scenario.
Mention the pre-outcome reduction from 16 to 14 scenes and the terminated v1 attempt in Section 4.5 or Appendix A.
Section 6: note that the 'toward centroid' and 'along generic shift' components of N overlap and are not additive.
State units of the centroid proximity gain in Table 11 (squared standardized units).
Report per-painter (not only name-averaged) proximity splits, since single-artist evaluations include cross terms that cancel only in the average.
Release the 1,008 generated images via an anonymous host or commit to release, enabling pixel-level re-extraction.
When correcting H for its 6.7% finite-sample bias, also report the implied Q and D.
Reduce numeric density in running text of Sections 5.3-5.4 for readability.
factual_errors: Intro bullet 5 and Section 5.5 heading: 'Texture is the least shared feature family' is false for GPT Image 2 and Sunburst (spatial lower) and Nano Banana 2 (texture highest, color lowest) per the paper's own Table 6.
Section 5.2: 'the observed shares are only a few points higher' than faithful; for GPT Image 2 in CLIP the observed share (73.2%) is below the faithful value (76.0%).
Abstract: proximity gain 'would remain' mostly shared for an exact imitator; the paper's own CSD faithful value for GPT Image 2 is 48.3% (a minority).

Figure 3 caption / Section 5.1: 'The observed fraction is below the faithful value in every configuration' is true only for point estimates; for FLUX.2 Max (31 features, 88.4 vs 90.4) the difference is not resolved under scene resampling.
